subject: Improvements to Multidim Mixture Model Specification?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Improvements to Multidim Mixture Model Specification?
parts:
Is this about as efficient as we can make a multidimensional mixture model?
There’s some additional complexity here in order to order the first component
of the means and (hopefully) identify the model.

data {
int<lower=0> D;
int<lower=0> K;
int<lower = 0> N;
vector[D] y[N];
}

transformed data {
matrix[D, D] L = diag_matrix(rep_vector(1, D));
}

parameters {
ordered[K] mu_head;
vector[D - 1] mu_tail[K];
simplex[K] lambda;
}

transformed parameters {
vector[D] mu[K];
for (k in 1:K) {
mu[k, 1] = mu_head[k];
mu[k, 2:D] = mu_tail[k];
}
}

model {
for (k in 1:K)
mu[k] ~ normal(0, 5);
lambda ~ beta(5, 5);
for (n in 1:N) {
vector[K] comp_lpdf;
for (k in 1:K) {
comp_lpdf[k] = log(lambda[k])
+ multi_normal_cholesky_lpdf(y[n] | mu[k], L);
}
target += log_sum_exp(comp_lpdf);
}
}

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: Improvements to Multidim Mixture Model Specification?
parts:
Follow-up: if you try to fit this model something odd happens.  Replacing the ordered vector mu_head with a regular vector and the model fits fine, covering to one of the degenerate modes.  But if you apply that ordering constrain then the three components all converge to around the weighted sum of the true means (1 * 0.45 + 5 * 0.35 - 4 * 0.2 = 1.4) as if the components all convolve with each other and cannot achieve distinct values.  

Needless to say, this is really weird.  Anyone have any ideas as to what is going on?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Improvements to Multidim Mixture Model Specification?
parts:
There's a bunch of things to improve for speed.

1. Add a log_lambda local in the model,

vector[K] log_lambda = log(lambda);

to avoid recomputation.

2. Not sure why you did it this way, but this
> matrix[D, D] L = diag_matrix(rep_vector(1, D));
and this

> comp_lpdf[k] = log(lambda[k])
> + multi_normal_cholesky_lpdf(y[n] | mu[k], L);

an be replaced with

comp_lpdf[k] = log_lambda[k] + normal_lpdf(y[n] | mu[k], 1);


3. vectorize

> for (k in 1:K)
> mu[k] ~ normal(0, 5);

as

mu ~ normal(0, 5);

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Improvements to Multidim Mixture Model Specification?
parts:
> On Apr 8, 2017, at 11:26 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Follow-up: if you try to fit this model something odd happens. Replacing the ordered vector mu_head with a regular vector and the model fits fine, covering to one of the degenerate modes. But if you apply that ordering constrain then the three components all converge to around the weighted sum of the true means (1 * 0.45 + 5 * 0.35 - 4 * 0.2 = 1.4) as if the components all convolve with each other and cannot achieve distinct values.
>
> Needless to say, this is really weird. Anyone have any ideas as to what is going on?

No idea how ordering could do this. The transform is just

x[1] = y[1],
x[n+1] = x[n] + exp(y[n])

with the obvious log Jacobian.

- Bob
